newsitem.title: GREECE: Nick Galis SA cleared for Athens bourse listing.
newsitem.headline: Nick Galis SA cleared for Athens bourse listing.

text.p: Nick Galis Youth Centres SA, owned by Greek basketball legend Nick Galis, has been cleared for listing on the Athens bourse's small-cap parallel market.

The company will issue 660,000 common registered shares with a par value of 200 drachmas at a price to be set by lead underwriter ABN-AMRO Bank shortly before the subscription book is opened in September.
But an issue price close to 800 drachmas should be expected, bringing the IPO proceeds to over 0.5 billion drachmas, company advisor D Finance told Reuters.
The company was founded in 1992 and is based in Thessaloniki, home of baskeball team Aris which Galis led to stardom in Europe in the 1980s and the early 1990s.
It operates Niko Magic Camp, a youth camping site and sports facility in a 65,000 square metre seaside plot leased from the municipality of Pefkohori on the Kassandra peninsula in northern Greece.
Proceeds from the share issue will finance the expansion of the youth centre and the construction of a 120-room nursing home for the elderly in the Thermi-Triadio area near Thessaloniki.
Current youth centre facilities have a capacity for 800 people, offering youngsters training in a wide variety of sports with accomplished trainers.

Niko Magic Camp is used as a training centre by a large number of sports teams and is also rated as an Adidas Europe Camp, which means that groups of children from all over Europe participate in athletic events staged at its premises.
The company saw its 1996 pretax profit rise 83.6 percent to 131 million drachmas on turnover growth of 32.6 percent to 364 million.
According to the IPO prospectus, earnings and turnover are forecast to grow 23 and 31 percent respectively in 1997 to 160 and 476 million drachmas. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
